negative_findings.description: Searched for Hungarian-language career/job pages for the international payments and self-service vendors most relevant to this market (Printec Hungary, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/NCR Atleos, Worldline, Euronet, Global Payments/SIX). No HU-localised careers URL surfaced for any of them; Printec Hungary Kft. appeared only as a company-registry record (OPTEN), not as a hiring page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor hiring in HU appears to run through global ATS instances and LinkedIn rather than HU career microsites; HU-language vendor career pages could not be confirmed to exist.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor market-entry signals must therefore be caught in English on global ATS/LinkedIn, and HU-language-only monitoring will systematically miss them.

negative_findings.description: Attempted to surface individual HU job ads that explicitly name a vendor platform (Temenos, Finastra, ACI, Backbase, OpenWay) in a Hungarian bank context. Search returned only vendor corporate/careers pages and generic aggregator pages, no concrete HU ad.
negative_findings.result_summary: Platform-named HU ads were not retrievable from open web search in this pass; they likely exist but are only visible inside board search interfaces and expire quickly.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that this cell cannot be served by search-engine queries alone — it needs in-board keyword search with scheduled snapshotting, since expired ads vanish from the index.

negative_findings.description: UniCredit Bank Hungary's dedicated HU career page did not surface in the bank career-page enumeration, unlike OTP, MBH, Erste, K&H and Raiffeisen.
negative_findings.result_summary: No UniCredit HU careers URL captured; presumed to route into the UniCredit group careers ATS.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Leaves a named top-tier HU bank uncovered in the employer watchlist.

negative_findings.description: Cvonline.hu is believed to sit in the Alma Career/CV Online group alongside other CEE boards, which would allow cross-border sibling-board monitoring, but this ownership structure was not confirmed in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Affects whether one collection recipe can be reused across CEE boards for regional vendor-entry signals.

coverage_gaps.description: Job ads are the most perishable source class in this run: HU board ads typically expire in 30-60 days and are then removed from both the board and the search index, so any signal not captured within the window is lost permanently.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up a weekly snapshot-and-diff collector over the watchlist (profession.hu keyword searches, each bank/GIRO/MNB ATS, vendor ATS country filters) with full-text archiving of ad bodies, not just titles.

coverage_gaps.description: The two highest-yield sources for vendor-side signals (LinkedIn Jobs, Glassdoor) are auth-walled and ToS-restricted, so they cannot be part of an automated pipeline.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Designate them as analyst-manual sources with a fixed weekly checklist of watchlist companies, or evaluate a licensed jobs-data provider for compliant coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Employer watchlist currently covers large banks, GIRO, MNB and a few HU software firms. Missing: UniCredit HU, CIB, Gránit, MagNet, MBH Fintechlab, Takarék entities, MFB, plus HU-based card processors, ATM independent deployers (Euronet HU), acquirers and PSPs, and the bank IT captives (e.g. Deutsche Telekom/IT Services Hungary, Diebold/NCR service partners).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Expand the watchlist using bankweb.hu's banki-állás directory and the MNB register of payment institutions, then attach each entity's career URL.

coverage_gaps.description: A stable HU keyword set for banking/payments job ads is only partially established (core banki rendszer, rendszerszervező, integrációs fejlesztő, POS terminál, ATM üzemeltetés, pénzforgalom, kártyarendszer, azonnali fizetés/AFR, qvik). Noisy terms not yet flagged: 'bank' matches non-financial employers, 'terminál' matches logistics, 'core' matches unrelated English-in-HU usage.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and version a HU/EN keyword file with precision weights and negative keywords before automating collection; validate recall against a hand-labelled sample of 50 ads.

coverage_gaps.description: No baseline exists for normal hiring volume per employer, so a spike (the actual weak signal) cannot yet be distinguished from routine churn or seasonal recruitment.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Collect at least two quarters of per-employer ad counts before drawing programme-level inferences; store counts as a time series alongside ad text.

brief: Hungarian hiring signals for banking and payments split into three tiers: first-party employer ATS (OTP, MBH, Erste, K&H, Raiffeisen, plus the two highest-signal infrastructure bodies GIRO Zrt. and MNB's toborzas.mnb.hu), the national job boards (profession.hu dominant, then cvonline.hu, jobline.hu, the IT-niche dreamjobs.hu and hwsw.hu), and aggregators (Indeed HU, Jooble, Jobmonitor, Állástérkép) that are best used as discovery pointers back to the canonical ad. Vendor-side entry signals are almost entirely English and live on global ATS instances (Temenos Workday, Diebold Nixdorf Oracle CX) and LinkedIn rather than any HU-localised career microsite, which is the main asymmetry in this cell. Consultancies and body-shops (Mindspire, Core Solutions, Hays, Randstad) act as pointer sources that convert anonymous demand into named programmes, with Mindspire's core-banking transformation blog unusually explicit. The binding constraint is ephemerality plus access: ads expire within weeks and the two richest vendor sources are auth-walled, so this cell only works as a scheduled snapshot-and-diff pipeline over the open sources with a manual analyst lane for LinkedIn and Glassdoor.
